identity.title: Identity

postures.noProxy: Shared token. No proxy names a person.
postures.anyVerified: Verified assertion (JWT), open to every identity

identity.approverRow: Write this exact value in an approver row.
identity.assertionMissing: A proxy is configured, and no verified identity reached this request. The gateway read the shared token instead, so every approval here names nobody. Check the proxy and the assertion header.
identity.plainCaution: The gateway reads this header and verifies nothing. The proxy alone decides who reaches the agent.
identity.anyVerifiedCaution: Every identity the provider signs for may reach the agent. allowAnyVerifiedIdentity is set.
identity.workspacePersonal: Yours. Files here are reachable by nobody else signed in to this deployment.
identity.workspaceShared: Shared. Everyone who reaches this gateway works in the same directory.
identity.signOutNote: The proxy in front holds the session, and this asks it to end it.

approvers.title: Approvers
approvers.empty: No approvers. No operator can approve an action at run time. An approve decision then refuses the action.
approvers.note: Membership in a channel allowFrom list grants nothing here. Only this list decides who can approve.
approvers.formNote: This panel adds no prefix. The gate compares the whole string, so it matches what you write here and nothing else.
approvers.webuiForm: The WebUI form is webui, or webui: and then the claim.
approvers.chatForm: The chat form is the account id of one person.
approvers.bareClaim: This sender is a bare claim, so it matches nobody. Write webui: and then the claim.
approvers.notAnAccountId: A chat approver is the numeric account id the channel gives.
approvers.blank: This row names no sender, so it matches nobody.

paths.title: Authenticated paths
paths.empty: No authenticated paths. No path can carry an approval, so every approve decision refuses the action.
paths.note: A path names a channel with a session concept. Two paths keep one account from both halves of an approval.

grants.title: Standing grants
grants.empty: No grants. No automation may run a remote command.
grants.expired: Expired {{when}}. The gate no longer matches it, and nothing removed the row.
grants.note: A grant permits a remote command and nothing else. It cannot permit an inventory write.

grantEditor.title: Standing grant
grantEditor.description: A grant permits one exact command on named hosts. It permits nothing else.
grantEditor.hostNote: These names come from inventory records. The gate compares the resolved address at run time, not the name.
grantEditor.commandNote: Exact match only. This field is not a pattern. A command that differs by one character does not match.

audit.title: Audit
audit.retentionHelp: The gate keeps each decision for this many days.
audit.fullTextWarning: Resolved commands often hold secrets. The log then holds them too.
audit.subtitle: One record per gate decision, newest first. The log appends, so this view reads only.
audit.samePath: The request and the approval arrived on one channel.
audit.samePathNote: The request and the approval arrived on one channel. One compromised account then holds both halves.
audit.originActorNote: The agent asserted who raised this action, and nothing authenticated that name. The actor is the other case: a trusted path authenticated the person who answered.
audit.textWarning: Full command text is on, so this record may hold a secret.
audit.empty: No decision matches these filters. The gate still records every decision it makes, so a wider range may show one.
audit.unreachable: This gateway cannot reach the audit log. The gate may still enforce every decision, so treat this as a missing view and not as an empty log.
audit.truncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} matching records. Narrow the filters to see the rest.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.subtitle: One human answer per action. The executor rendered every byte below.
approvals.empty: No action waits for an answer. Policy still refuses every action it refuses, so an empty inbox is not an open gate.
approvals.degraded: The gateway cannot reach the executor. An action may wait, and this list cannot show it.
approvals.unavailable: This gateway holds no approvals inbox. An approve decision waits for the deadline and then refuses.
approvals.expiresNote: At zero the executor refuses this action. The agent gets no retry.
approvals.expired: This action expired. The executor refused it.
approvals.payloadTitle: Command and hosts, exactly as the executor will run them
approvals.payloadNote: The executor produced this text. The agent did not describe it.
approvals.contextDivider: The lines below are context. The digest does not cover them.

grant.menuLabel: Approve and add a standing grant
grant.menuNote: Adds a standing grant for this exact command on these hosts. A command that differs by one flag is a different command.
grant.add24h: Approve and add — expires in 24 hours
grant.add7d: Approve and add — expires in 7 days
grant.permanentTitle: Add a grant that never expires?
grant.permanentBody: This command runs on these hosts from now on, with nobody asked. The grant stays until you remove it in Settings → Security.
grant.savedPermanent: Standing grant {{id}} added, and it never expires. Remove it in Settings → Security.
grant.notSaved: The action was approved. The grant was not saved: {{reason}}

approvals.samePath: This request came from the path you are on. Approve it from another authenticated path. One compromised account must not supply both halves.
approvals.denyTerminal: A denial is terminal for this session. The agent cannot ask again until an operator clears the latch.
approvals.approved: You approved this action. The executor runs it now.
approvals.denied: You denied this action. The denial is terminal for this session.
approvals.noAnswer: The gateway did not answer. The action still waits.

refusal.alreadyAnswered: This action already has an answer. One action takes one answer.
refusal.digestMismatch: Your answer covers other bytes. Reload this page, read the payload again, then answer.
refusal.expired: This action expired before your answer arrived. The executor refused it.
refusal.noSecondPath: Only one authenticated path exists. Add a second path, or declare a standing grant.
refusal.notAnApprover: This account is not in gates.approvers. Add it to that list, then answer again.
refusal.samePath: This request came from the path you are on. Answer it from another authenticated path.
refusal.unauthenticatedPath: gates.approvalPaths does not list webui, so this path authenticates no approver.
refusal.unknownOriginPath: The request names no origin path. The executor cannot prove path independence.
refusal.unknownRequest: The executor does not hold this request. It expired, or somebody answered it.

approvals.agentAsserted: The agent named itself. That is a claim of the request, not an identity this deployment authenticated, and the digest above does not cover it.
approvals.agentDefaultNote: No agent named itself, so this deployment's default agent runs it. That too is the request's own account of itself rather than an authenticated identity, and the digest above does not cover it.

serverNotes.title: Device notes
serverNotes.hint: What a future visitor to this box needs to know. A note does not expire — one that disagrees with what you see is evidence the infrastructure changed.
serverNotes.empty: No notes yet — the agent writes here when it learns something.
serverNotes.bodyPlaceholder: The conclusion, and what not to 'fix'.
serverNotes.authorNote: Signed as the operator, with your verified identity.

roster.emptyHelp: No agent is named yet, so every message is answered by the agent above. Name one to give it its own model, its own tools and its own instructions, addressed as @agent:<name>.
roster.deleteDescription: The agent stops existing and stops being addressable. Past messages stay in their sessions.
roster.deleteDependents: {{agents}} delegate to this agent. Config refuses a roster whose delegate does not exist, so remove it from them first.
roster.chipAllHelp: Nothing declared, which is every one of them.
roster.defaultHelp: What answers when no agent is chosen, and what every named agent inherits from.
roster.defaultModelFact: The preset this deployment activates. Changing it changes every agent that names none of its own.
roster.defaultNotEditable: This agent cannot be added, renamed or removed: it is what a deployment has before it names anything. This page writes named agents only, and the default agent's own settings live in the other Settings panels.
roster.defaultPromptFact: The platform's own sections, with nothing added and nothing replaced.
roster.defaultToolGroupsFact: Every tool group, because declaring none is how config says all of them.
roster.promptCustomHelp: This agent adds to or replaces the platform's own prompt. The Prompt tab shows which sections.
roster.promptDefaultHelp: This agent is told what the platform says, with nothing added or replaced.
roster.subtitle: Manage AI agents
roster.chipNoneHelp: Declared, and empty: this agent reaches none of them.

prompt.unavailable: This gateway does not report the prompt composition.
prompt.replacedHelp: This deployment replaced the platform's text for this section. The section is still named here, because a record that hid the replacement would make two different prompts look identical.
prompt.estimateNote: Token figures are estimates for the sections that cost the same on every turn. What one turn actually carried is on the turn itself.

permissionHelp.replaceable: This section is the deployment's own text to write.
permissionHelp.workspace: Already yours by another route: the workspace's own instruction files.
permissionHelp.derived: Computed from config, so config is where it changes.
permissionHelp.appendOnly: Added after the platform's sections; it can replace none of them.
permissionHelp.fixed: The tool contract and the safety notes. Deleting them would leave the gate refusing actions the model no longer knows the rules for.

prompt.addendumPlaceholder: Prefer read-only checks, and say what you did not check.
prompt.unsaved: The prompt sections appear once this agent is saved.
prompt.addendumElsewhere: The addendum is edited on the Basic tab.
prompt.emptyIsDefault: An empty section is not something config can store, so saving this restores the platform's own text.
prompt.introHelp: Every section of the system prompt, in the order the platform assembles it. The pencil opens a section's text for editing, and editing is the only way to remove something the platform says -- an addendum can add to it but never take it back. The sections without a pencil are built from your config or from the workspace, so they change there.
prompt.noDefaultText: The platform assembles this section on every turn, so there is no default text to start from. What you write here stands in its place.
prompt.perTurnBody: The platform assembles this section on every turn, from the workspace and the session, so there is no fixed text to show here.
prompt.placeholders: Keep these placeholders in your text:
prompt.sectionEmpty: This section carries nothing for this agent.

editor.nameHelp: How the agent is addressed in a message, as @agent:<name>. Letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'.
editor.nameFixedHelp: An agent keeps the name it was created with: automations and threads address it by that name.
editor.descriptionHelp: The line that explains this agent wherever it is offered, including to another agent deciding whether to delegate.
editor.toolGroupsHelp: Everything means no ceiling. Only these narrows the agent to the groups you pick — and picking none is how an agent is told it must ask a peer for anything grouped.
editor.toolGroupsEmpty: This deployment has no tool groups yet.
editor.mcpServersEmpty: This deployment installs no MCP servers.
editor.bindingHelp: Everything is whatever this deployment activates. Only these narrows this agent to what you pick, and never widens it — an empty pick is an agent that loads none of them, which is what a schema budget is spent on.
editor.skillsHelp: Everything summarises the whole catalogue, as before. Only these loads what you pick in full and summarises nothing else — which is what keeps a conversation from paying for every skill installed.
editor.delegatesHelp: The agents this one may hand work to. Membership is the authorization, so an agent reaches only the peers named here.
editor.delegatesEmpty: There is no other agent to delegate to yet.
editor.duplicate: {{name}} already exists. Saving would replace it, so open that agent instead.
editor.staleGateway: This gateway reports how many tool groups, skills and delegates {{name}} has but not which ones, so saving would replace them with nothing. Update the gateway to edit this agent here.
editor.addendumHelp: Appended after the platform's own sections. It can only add: a sentence you disagree with cannot be undone by appending a correction, because the model is handed both. To remove one, edit that section on the Prompt tab.
editor.modelPresetHelp: Which of this deployment's model presets answers for this agent. A preset carries the model, the provider and the limits together, so there is nothing to keep in step by hand.
editor.providerHelp: Decided by the preset, not chosen here: a preset names the model and the provider that serves it together.
editor.bindingAllNote: Nothing declared: this agent reaches every one this deployment has, and gains any you add later.
editor.bindingNoneNote: Declared and empty: this agent reaches none of them.

defaults.reachesEveryTurn: What you write here is added to the system prompt of every turn that names no agent — which is every turn, in a deployment that names none.
defaults.scope: This agent cannot be added, renamed or removed: it is what a deployment has before it names anything. Everything else about it is edited here, like any other agent. Its deployment settings — the timezone, the tool-iteration cap, the subagent limit — live in the panels that own them.
defaults.staleGateway: This gateway does not report the default agent's addendum, replaced sections or bindings, so saving would replace them with what this form never read. Update the gateway to edit them here.
defaults.toolGroupsHelp: Everything is what a deployment has before it narrows anything. Only these caps every turn that names no agent — the tools outside the groups you pick are not offered and a call to one is refused.
defaults.mcpHelp: This is the one that costs the most. Every installed server's schemas load in the first message of every conversation, so Only these is how a deployment with a dozen of them stops paying for eleven.
defaults.connectorsHelp: Everything is whatever this deployment activates. Only these narrows the turn to the connectors you pick, and never widens it.
defaults.skillsHelp: Everything summarises the whole catalogue, as before. Only these loads what you pick in full and summarises nothing else — the catalogue itself is what a long list of skills spends.
defaults.skillsNoneNote: Declared and empty: no skill loads and no catalogue is summarised either.
defaults.skillsVsDisabled: Separate from the skills this deployment disables, in Settings → Skills. That list removes a skill from every agent; this one chooses which of what remains this agent loads in full.
defaults.delegatesHelp: The agents this one may hand work to. It matters most here: this is the agent you talk to, so without a peer named the only way to reach one is to stop talking to it.
defaults.delegatesEmpty: This deployment names no other agent yet.
